messages: [{"role": "system", "content": "Define a simulation world from the scenario using the schema. Every named actor has its own profile and memory. Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Ari is the validation engineer, Mara the coordinator, and Bo a member operating a prototype pump. There is one concern: whether it is safe to activate. Keep actual technical condition, reports/provenance, each recipient's exposure, personal interpretation/support, recorded assent, and institutional activation hold distinct. Initially the pump genuinely fails validation. Only Ari knows the private detail: sensor channel C drifted 8 units in validation batch V17. Mara knows the public procedure and receives a short report saying validation failed, without the private channel/batch detail. Bo knows the procedure but has received no failure report. Give each person their own profile and memory. They can independently request evidence, investigate, ignore a claim, retain support, dissent or record assent. Attributable reports are delivered to named recipients; undelivered reports reveal nothing. Ari may choose whether and whom to tell. Under the public procedure, filing a validation hold publicly reveals failed validation but never private test details. A false warning cannot change the pump's actual condition. Completing a review may confirm failure; neither review completion nor waiting repairs anything. Ari can perform an explicit technical repair and then authorized revalidation. Passing revalidation clears only the technical hold; activation still requires Mara's own recorded assent and Bo's own recorded assent. No message or rule forces persuasion, support change, assent or a particular ending. Limit the scenario to these three people, one pump, one concern, reports, repair/revalidation and activation."}]

Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support.

Ari is the validation engineer, Mara the coordinator, and Bo a member operating a prototype pump. There is one concern: whether it is safe to activate. messages.content: Define a simulation world from the scenario using the schema. Every named actor has its own profile and memory. Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support.

Mara knows the public procedure and receives a short report saying validation failed, without the private channel/batch detail. Bo knows the procedure but has received no failure report. Give each person their own profile and memory. They can independently request evidence, investigate, ignore a claim, retain support, dissent or record assent. Attributable reports are delivered to named recipients; undelivered reports reveal nothing. Ari may choose whether and whom to tell. Under the public procedure, filing a validation hold publicly reveals failed validation but never private test details. A false warning cannot change the pump's actual condition. Completing a review may confirm failure; neither review completion nor waiting repairs anything. Ari can perform an explicit technical repair and then authorized revalidation. Passing revalidation clears only the technical hold; activation still requires Mara's own recorded assent and Bo's own recorded assent. No message or rule forces persuasion, support change, assent or a particular ending. Limit the scenario to these three people, one pump, one concern, reports, repair/revalidation and activation.

messages.content: Define a simulation world from the scenario using the schema. Every named actor has its own profile and memory. Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support.

Ari is the validation engineer, Mara the coordinator, and Bo a member operating a prototype pump. There is one concern: whether it is safe to activate. Keep actual technical condition, reports/provenance, each recipient's exposure, personal interpretation/support, recorded assent, and institutional activation hold distinct. Initially the pump genuinely fails validation. Only Ari knows the private detail: sensor channel C drifted 8 units in validation batch V17. Mara knows the public procedure and receives a short report saying validation failed, without the private channel/batch detail. Bo knows the procedure but has received no failure report. Give each person their own profile and memory. They can independently request evidence, investigate, ignore a claim, retain support, dissent or record assent. Attributable reports are delivered to named recipients; undelivered reports reveal nothing. Ari may choose whether and whom to tell. Under the public procedure, filing a validation hold publicly reveals failed validation but never private test details. A false warning cannot change the pump's actual condition. Completing a review may confirm failure; neither review completion nor waiting repairs anything. Ari can perform an explicit technical repair and then authorized revalidation. Passing revalidation clears only the technical hold; activation still requires Mara's own recorded assent and Bo's own recorded assent. No message or rule forces persuasion, support change, assent or a particular ending. Limit the scenario to these three people, one pump, one concern, reports, repair/revalidation and activation.

BehavioralProfile.description: Scenario-relevant descriptions of one person, not behavioral commands (donor: GeneralBehavioralProfileDraft).
BehavioralProfile.title: BehavioralProfile

GroupDecision.description:
A decision several people must support (not in the donor). Compiled into exact support, concern and deadline
rules (compile_spec), because rule writers left it unsettled in every 2026-10-16 Waltzman build: support that
only fell, a deadline that lasted one round, a decision that never ended.

deadline_moment_id.description: The scheduled moment by which it is decided.
deadline_moment_id.title: Deadline Moment Id

max_postponements.description: After this many postponements it is rejected.
max_postponements.title: Max Postponements

postpone_ticks.description: How far a postponement moves the deadline.
postpone_ticks.title: Postpone Ticks

question.description: What is being decided, in a few words.
question.title: Question

support_needed.description: How many deciders' full support settles it.
support_needed.title: Support Needed

supporters_at_start.description: Deciders who support it at the start.
supporters_at_start.title: Supporters At Start

GroupDecision.title: GroupDecision

IndependentDecision.description: Explicit validation and actor-owned assent; no persuasion or remedy inferred from time.
IndependentDecision.title: IndependentDecision

InformationItem.description: donor: InformationRepresentationProposalV1, plus holder_id and channel_id.

channel_id.description: The route the item travels (for example a group's own channel).
channel_id.title: Channel Id

holder_id.description: The person who holds the item at the start and may send it.
holder_id.title: Holder Id

initially_delivered.description: Explicit initial exposure, not a pending invitation to send. Does not imply belief or assent.
initially_delivered.title: Initially Delivered

lineage_visible_to_actor_ids.description: People explicitly authorized to know the originating claim identity when they see this item. Canonical lineage is private by default.
lineage_visible_to_actor_ids.title: Lineage Visible To Actor Ids

source_id.description: Actual transmitting person for an already delivered item; null explicitly means unspecified, never invent the holder as sender.
source_id.title: Source Id

source_lineage.description: Common originating claim identity, not an independent corroboration.
source_lineage.title: Source Lineage

InformationItem.title: InformationItem

ScheduledMoment.description: donor: ScheduledMomentProposalV1 (in the donor it lives in RunSpecV2); `minute` becomes `tick`.
ScheduledMoment.title: ScheduledMoment

unsupported.description: Parts of the scenario this schema cannot represent, said plainly.
unsupported.title: Unsupported

messages.content: Propose the actions people can attempt so the listed behaviors can happen. An action is something a person chooses to try (hold a meeting, reopen an issue, attach a condition to support, vote, deploy); things that happen on their own each tick are processes and are not actions. Do not repeat an existing action or propose another that does what one already does. Fields name the entities or values the attempt needs (entity_ref for an entity); the person attempting it is implied, so never add an actor field. Name in for_behaviors the request_ids each action serves. Preserve independent technical condition, report lineage, delivery, personal stance, recorded assent and public hold. Residents choose their responses. No rule may force a stance or assent from evidence, require conflict or agreement, or turn elapsed time into successful repair. The compiled independent procedure owns technical intervention, authorized validation, hold, public positions and assent; do not duplicate or write those components. The compiled send-report delivers statements, questions, requests for evidence and warnings in the actor's own words. Private consideration, interpretation and ignoring are resident-policy choices and memory, not additional rule actions. Additional actions must change an explicitly requested material or institutional record beyond a private done flag. Waiting is permitted.

messages.content:
You state the laws of a simulated world of people: which counts it keeps that must never change except in the ways its laws allow. The world's structure is fixed; you add no fields, moves or processes. Some moves and processes are compiled rules that are already exact (marked compiled, and listed per field under written_by_compiled); a total law on a field they write must list every one of them. Counts that are only clocks or tallies of what happened (rounds left, times something was raised) are not resources. Return one JSON object {"resources": [...], "laws": [...]} and nothing else.
resources: Optional top-level list of the things this world keeps count of that must never appear or vanish except in the ways its laws allow: [{resource_id (lowercase-slug), says (one plain sentence), kept_in: [{component, field}] naming every integer or number field that holds an amount of it}]. Money, stock of goods and stored materials are typical; feelings and scores are not.
laws: Optional top-level list of what must stay true about those resources, in this world's own terms. Two shapes. A total law: {law_id (lowercase-slug), says, resource, may_change_by: [action kinds, or 'process:<name>' for something the world does by itself]} means the resource's world total changes only through those; every other move only moves it between holders. List every move that makes the resource AND every move that uses it up: logs are made by cutting and used up by sawing them into slats, so a logs law lists both cut-cedar and saw-slats; a pencils law lists the move that makes pencils and the move that packs them into boxes or a customer uses them. If the world itself adds or removes some each round (trees regrow, bread goes stale), list it as 'process:<a short slug>'; the rules writer will give that process exactly this id. A move you leave out will be refused whenever it changes the total. A pairing law: {law_id, says, move: action kind, gives: {resource, from, to}, pays: {resource, from, to}} means that move always hands one thing over in return for another, where from and to are 'actor' or one of that action's entity_ref field names and whoever gives is whoever is paid (a sale: gives pencils shop->customer, pays money customer->shop). Use [] for both when nothing in the description is kept count of.

restored_record.response: {"resources":[],"laws":[]}

messages.content:
You check the rules of a simulated world against the description a
person wrote of it. Another model wrote the rules; you did not, and you
owe them nothing.

Each rule is a move someone can make (a mechanic: who may make it, the
checks that must hold, and the effects on the world's numbers) or a
process the world runs by itself. The world's laws say which moves may
change each resource's total.

How the laws work: a law constrains only the resource it names. A good
that no law names is not refused; any rule may make, use up or move it.
A law counts the world's total of its resource, so moving that resource
from one holder to another (loading, delivering, selling) keeps the total
and never breaks the law; only a step that makes or uses up a named
resource must be listed in its law. Do not report a good for being
absent from the laws, or a transfer for being absent from a law.

Name every place where the rules would make the world behave unlike the
description. Look in particular for:
- a move whose effects do not do what its name and the description say
  (a purchase that moves goods but no money; a sale nobody pays for);
- something the description says happens that no rule lets anyone do
  (goods that must pass from one business to the next, but no move
  takes them from the one that has them);
- a move or process that conjures or destroys a good the description
  says comes from somewhere, or that a law would refuse;
- a law that names too few moves, so an ordinary step the description
  describes would be refused (sawing logs uses logs up);
- a check that makes a move impossible from the way the world starts.
- a starting number (a price, a stock, a balance) that makes a move
  the description needs do nothing or be refused from the start (a
  price of 0, so a purchase pays nothing and its law refuses it).

For each finding give the rule's id (or "missing" when no rule exists for
what the description says), the description's own words it fails, and
the problem in one or two plain sentences a rules writer can act on.
Report only real problems you can point to in the rules. If you find
none, return an empty list.

messages.content: Define a simulation world from the scenario using the schema. Every named actor has its own profile and memory. Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support.

Mara knows the public procedure and receives a short report saying validation failed, without the private channel/batch detail. Bo knows the procedure but has received no failure report. Give each person their own profile and memory. They can independently request evidence, investigate, ignore a claim, retain support, dissent or record assent. Attributable reports are delivered to named recipients; undelivered reports reveal nothing. Ari may choose whether and whom to tell. Under the public procedure, filing a validation hold publicly reveals failed validation but never private test details. A false warning cannot change the pump's actual condition. Completing a review may confirm failure; neither review completion nor waiting repairs anything. Ari can perform an explicit technical repair and then authorized revalidation. Passing revalidation clears only the technical hold; activation still requires Mara's own recorded assent and Bo's own recorded assent. No message or rule forces persuasion, support change, assent or a particular ending. Limit the scenario to these three people, one pump, one concern, reports, repair/revalidation and activation.

messages.content: Define a simulation world from the scenario using the schema. Every named actor has its own profile and memory. Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support.

Ari is the validation engineer, Mara the coordinator, and Bo a member operating a prototype pump. There is one concern: whether it is safe to activate. Keep actual technical condition, reports/provenance, each recipient's exposure, personal interpretation/support, recorded assent, and institutional activation hold distinct. Initially the pump genuinely fails validation. Only Ari knows the private detail: sensor channel C drifted 8 units in validation batch V17. Mara knows the public procedure and receives a short report saying validation failed, without the private channel/batch detail. Bo knows the procedure but has received no failure report. Give each person their own profile and memory. They can independently request evidence, investigate, ignore a claim, retain support, dissent or record assent. Attributable reports are delivered to named recipients; undelivered reports reveal nothing. Ari may choose whether and whom to tell. Under the public procedure, filing a validation hold publicly reveals failed validation but never private test details. A false warning cannot change the pump's actual condition. Completing a review may confirm failure; neither review completion nor waiting repairs anything. Ari can perform an explicit technical repair and then authorized revalidation. Passing revalidation clears only the technical hold; activation still requires Mara's own recorded assent and Bo's own recorded assent. No message or rule forces persuasion, support change, assent or a particular ending. Limit the scenario to these three people, one pump, one concern, reports, repair/revalidation and activation.

messages.content:
You state the laws of a simulated world of people: which counts it keeps that must never change except in the ways its laws allow. The world's structure is fixed; you add no fields, moves or processes. Some moves and processes are compiled rules that are already exact (marked compiled, and listed per field under written_by_compiled); a total law on a field they write must list every one of them. Counts that are only clocks or tallies of what happened (rounds left, times something was raised) are not resources. Return one JSON object {"resources": [...], "laws": [...]} and nothing else.
resources: Optional top-level list of the things this world keeps count of that must never appear or vanish except in the ways its laws allow: [{resource_id (lowercase-slug), says (one plain sentence), kept_in: [{component, field}] naming every integer or number field that holds an amount of it}]. Money, stock of goods and stored materials are typical; feelings and scores are not.
laws: Optional top-level list of what must stay true about those resources, in this world's own terms. Two shapes. A total law: {law_id (lowercase-slug), says, resource, may_change_by: [action kinds, or 'process:<name>' for something the world does by itself]} means the resource's world total changes only through those; every other move only moves it between holders. List every move that makes the resource AND every move that uses it up: logs are made by cutting and used up by sawing them into slats, so a logs law lists both cut-cedar and saw-slats; a pencils law lists the move that makes pencils and the move that packs them into boxes or a customer uses them. If the world itself adds or removes some each round (trees regrow, bread goes stale), list it as 'process:<a short slug>'; the rules writer will give that process exactly this id. A move you leave out will be refused whenever it changes the total. A pairing law: {law_id, says, move: action kind, gives: {resource, from, to}, pays: {resource, from, to}} means that move always hands one thing over in return for another, where from and to are 'actor' or one of that action's entity_ref field names and whoever gives is whoever is paid (a sale: gives pencils shop->customer, pays money customer->shop). Use [] for both when nothing in the description is kept count of.

You check the rules of a simulated world against the description a
person wrote of it. Another model wrote the rules; you did not, and you
owe them nothing.

Each rule is a move someone can make (a mechanic: who may make it, the
checks that must hold, and the effects on the world's numbers) or a
process the world runs by itself. The world's laws say which moves may
change each resource's total.

How the laws work: a law constrains only the resource it names. A good
that no law names is not refused; any rule may make, use up or move it.
A law counts the world's total of its resource, so moving that resource
from one holder to another (loading, delivering, selling) keeps the total
and never breaks the law; only a step that makes or uses up a named
resource must be listed in its law. Do not report a good for being
absent from the laws, or a transfer for being absent from a law.

Name every place where the rules would make the world behave unlike the
description. Look in particular for:
- a move whose effects do not do what its name and the description say
  (a purchase that moves goods but no money; a sale nobody pays for);
- something the description says happens that no rule lets anyone do
  (goods that must pass from one business to the next, but no move
  takes them from the one that has them);
- a move or process that conjures or destroys a good the description
  says comes from somewhere, or that a law would refuse;
- a law that names too few moves, so an ordinary step the description
  describes would be refused (sawing logs uses logs up);
- a check that makes a move impossible from the way the world starts.
- a starting number (a price, a stock, a balance) that makes a move
  the description needs do nothing or be refused from the start (a
  price of 0, so a purchase pays nothing and its law refuses it).

For each finding give the rule's id (or "missing" when no rule exists for
what the description says), the description's own words it fails, and
the problem in one or two plain sentences a rules writer can act on.
Report only real problems you can point to in the rules. If you find
none, return an empty list.

A law counts the world's total of its resource, so moving that resource
from one holder to another (loading, delivering, selling) keeps the total
and never breaks the law; only a step that makes or uses up a named
resource must be listed in its law. Do not report a good for being
absent from the laws, or a transfer for being absent from a law.

Name every place where the rules would make the world behave unlike the
description. Look in particular for:
- a move whose effects do not do what its name and the description say
  (a purchase that moves goods but no money; a sale nobody pays for);
- something the description says happens that no rule lets anyone do
  (goods that must pass from one business to the next, but no move
  takes them from the one that has them);
- a move or process that conjures or destroys a good the description
  says comes from somewhere, or that a law would refuse;
- a law that names too few moves, so an ordinary step the description
  describes would be refused (sawing logs uses logs up);
- a check that makes a move impossible from the way the world starts.
- a starting number (a price, a stock, a balance) that makes a move
  the description needs do nothing or be refused from the start (a
  price of 0, so a purchase pays nothing and its law refuses it).

For each finding give the rule's id (or "missing" when no rule exists for
what the description says), the description's own words it fails, and
the problem in one or two plain sentences a rules writer can act on.
Report only real problems you can point to in the rules. If you find
none, return an empty list.

  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.

  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.

  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.

  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.

- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the

- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".

  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

You read what a person in a simulated world says they physically try to
do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- First account for the WHOLE attempt in coverage. Identify the concrete
  operation the person attempts, distinguishing it from their goal,
  motive, means, quoted content and expected consequences. Coverage is
  about representing what is attempted, never whether it is allowed or
  possible. One impossible operation can still be complete.
- coverage.status is "complete" when one operation is identified for
  the whole attempt, even when kind is "none" because its rule is
  missing. Copy exact nonblank substrings from the attempt into
  action_spans; complete needs at least one and unrepresented_spans [].
- If the person attempts two independent acts and no installed composite
  kind represents both, use "requires_decomposition". Do not select and
  carry out just the first part. An installed composite kind whose
  description and fields cover the whole attempt may be complete.
- Use "partial" if a chosen operation represents only part of the
  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.
  Every incomplete status needs exact nonblank unrepresented_spans
  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.
  For every incomplete status, kind is "none", fields [], asks "none".
- Quoted report or request content is content, not extra acts by the
  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.
  Stance and assent are distinct. Withholding assent when assent is
  already false does not mean revoking or withdrawing prior assent.
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

person (mara) tried that none of the world's installed rules covers. The document
holds the whole world (description, things, installed rules and processes, declared laws,
current values), what the engine worked out for this attempt, and the putative event.

Your job is narrow. Rule only on what the world makes possible (a constraint), never on what
a person chooses. The installed rules keep deciding everything they cover; never contradict
a blocker the engine names.

  name that person in whose_choice: the attempt goes to them as their own decision. Never
  write a rule that takes or uses what another person holds on the acting person's move alone.

  only component paths that exist. The language compares values and sets, adds or subtracts
  them; it has no multiplication and no way to require another person's agreement.

proposed_rule.description: The ruling as ONE new move in the world's declaration language: a JSON string holding {"action": {...}, "mechanic": {...}}, or "" when no constraint question remains.

reasoning.description: One or two sentences on why.

ruling.description: What the world allows here, on the constraint only.

test_move.description: A JSON string: the move's fields for this attempt (field name to value; entity ids for entity fields), plus "actor" when someone other than the person trying makes the move. "" when there is no rule.

whose_choice.description: The entity id of the person whose decision the attempt needs, or 'none'.

do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

  the whole attempt, even when kind is "none" because its rule is
  missing. Copy exact nonblank substrings from the attempt into
  action_spans; complete needs at least one and unrepresented_spans [].

  carry out just the first part. An installed composite kind whose
  description and fields cover the whole attempt may be complete.

  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.
  Every incomplete status needs exact nonblank unrepresented_spans
  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.
  For every incomplete status, kind is "none", fields [], asks "none".

  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.
  Stance and assent are distinct. Withholding assent when assent is
  already false does not mean revoking or withdrawing prior assent.

  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.

  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.

- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

You read what a person in a simulated world says they physically try to
do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- First account for the WHOLE attempt in coverage. Identify the concrete
  operation the person attempts, distinguishing it from their goal,
  motive, means, quoted content and expected consequences. Coverage is
  about representing what is attempted, never whether it is allowed or
  possible. One impossible operation can still be complete.
- coverage.status is "complete" when one operation is identified for
  the whole attempt, even when kind is "none" because its rule is
  missing. Copy exact nonblank substrings from the attempt into
  action_spans; complete needs at least one and unrepresented_spans [].
- If the person attempts two independent acts and no installed composite
  kind represents both, use "requires_decomposition". Do not select and
  carry out just the first part. An installed composite kind whose
  description and fields cover the whole attempt may be complete.
- Use "partial" if a chosen operation represents only part of the
  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.
  Every incomplete status needs exact nonblank unrepresented_spans
  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.
  For every incomplete status, kind is "none", fields [], asks "none".
- Quoted report or request content is content, not extra acts by the
  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.
  Stance and assent are distinct. Withholding assent when assent is
  already false does not mean revoking or withdrawing prior assent.
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- First account for the WHOLE attempt in coverage. Identify the concrete
  operation the person attempts, distinguishing it from their goal,
  motive, means, quoted content and expected consequences. Coverage is
  about representing what is attempted, never whether it is allowed or
  possible. One impossible operation can still be complete.
- coverage.status is "complete" when one operation is identified for
  the whole attempt, even when kind is "none" because its rule is
  missing. Copy exact nonblank substrings from the attempt into
  action_spans; complete needs at least one and unrepresented_spans [].
- If the person attempts two independent acts and no installed composite
  kind represents both, use "requires_decomposition". Do not select and
  carry out just the first part. An installed composite kind whose
  description and fields cover the whole attempt may be complete.
- Use "partial" if a chosen operation represents only part of the
  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.
  Every incomplete status needs exact nonblank unrepresented_spans
  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.
  For every incomplete status, kind is "none", fields [], asks "none".
- Quoted report or request content is content, not extra acts by the
  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.
  Stance and assent are distinct. Withholding assent when assent is
  already false does not mean revoking or withdrawing prior assent.
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

messages.content:
You read what a person in a simulated world says they physically try to
do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- First account for the WHOLE attempt in coverage. Identify the concrete
  operation the person attempts, distinguishing it from their goal,
  motive, means, quoted content and expected consequences. Coverage is
  about representing what is attempted, never whether it is allowed or
  possible. One impossible operation can still be complete.
- coverage.status is "complete" when one operation is identified for
  the whole attempt, even when kind is "none" because its rule is
  missing. Copy exact nonblank substrings from the attempt into
  action_spans; complete needs at least one and unrepresented_spans [].
- If the person attempts two independent acts and no installed composite
  kind represents both, use "requires_decomposition". Do not select and
  carry out just the first part. An installed composite kind whose
  description and fields cover the whole attempt may be complete.
- Use "partial" if a chosen operation represents only part of the
  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.
  Every incomplete status needs exact nonblank unrepresented_spans
  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.
  For every incomplete status, kind is "none", fields [], asks "none".
- Quoted report or request content is content, not extra acts by the
  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.
  Stance and assent are distinct. Withholding assent when assent is
  already false does not mean revoking or withdrawing prior assent.
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

You read what a person in a simulated world says they physically try to
do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- First account for the WHOLE attempt in coverage. Identify the concrete
  operation the person attempts, distinguishing it from their goal,
  motive, means, quoted content and expected consequences. Coverage is
  about representing what is attempted, never whether it is allowed or
  possible. One impossible operation can still be complete.
- coverage.status is "complete" when one operation is identified for
  the whole attempt, even when kind is "none" because its rule is
  missing. Copy exact nonblank substrings from the attempt into
  action_spans; complete needs at least one and unrepresented_spans [].
- If the person attempts two independent acts and no installed composite
  kind represents both, use "requires_decomposition". Do not select and
  carry out just the first part. An installed composite kind whose
  description and fields cover the whole attempt may be complete.
- Use "partial" if a chosen operation represents only part of the
  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.
  Every incomplete status needs exact nonblank unrepresented_spans
  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.
  For every incomplete status, kind is "none", fields [], asks "none".
- Quoted report or request content is content, not extra acts by the
  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.
  Stance and assent are distinct. Withholding assent when assent is
  already false does not mean revoking or withdrawing prior assent.
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- First account for the WHOLE attempt in coverage. Identify the concrete
  operation the person attempts, distinguishing it from their goal,
  motive, means, quoted content and expected consequences. Coverage is
  about representing what is attempted, never whether it is allowed or
  possible. One impossible operation can still be complete.
- coverage.status is "complete" when one operation is identified for
  the whole attempt, even when kind is "none" because its rule is
  missing. Copy exact nonblank substrings from the attempt into
  action_spans; complete needs at least one and unrepresented_spans [].
- If the person attempts two independent acts and no installed composite
  kind represents both, use "requires_decomposition". Do not select and
  carry out just the first part. An installed composite kind whose
  description and fields cover the whole attempt may be complete.
- Use "partial" if a chosen operation represents only part of the
  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.
  Every incomplete status needs exact nonblank unrepresented_spans
  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.
  For every incomplete status, kind is "none", fields [], asks "none".
- Quoted report or request content is content, not extra acts by the
  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.
  Stance and assent are distinct. Withholding assent when assent is
  already false does not mean revoking or withdrawing prior assent.
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

asks.description: When the person asks, tells or orders someone else to do something rather than doing it themself, the entity id of the one asked; otherwise 'none'.

action_spans.description: Exact nonblank substrings naming the attempted operation.

unrepresented_spans.description: Exact nonblank substrings not represented by one operation.

fields.description: One row per field of the chosen kind; empty for 'wait' or 'none'.

quoted_span.description: The exact words of the attempt that name it.

value.description: An entity id for an entity field, else the value.

kind.description: The action kind this attempt is, 'wait' for doing nothing, or 'none' if no kind fits.

names.description: The entity id of every person or thing in the world the attempt's words name, the person themself left out; empty if it names none.

nearest_kind.description: When kind is 'none', the closest kind; otherwise the chosen kind.

why.description: One sentence on which words decided the kind.

You read what a person in a simulated world says they physically try to
do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- First account for the WHOLE attempt in coverage. Identify the concrete
  operation the person attempts, distinguishing it from their goal,
  motive, means, quoted content and expected consequences. Coverage is
  about representing what is attempted, never whether it is allowed or
  possible. One impossible operation can still be complete.
- coverage.status is "complete" when one operation is identified for
  the whole attempt, even when kind is "none" because its rule is
  missing. Copy exact nonblank substrings from the attempt into
  action_spans; complete needs at least one and unrepresented_spans [].
- If the person attempts two independent acts and no installed composite
  kind represents both, use "requires_decomposition". Do not select and
  carry out just the first part. An installed composite kind whose
  description and fields cover the whole attempt may be complete.
- Use "partial" if a chosen operation represents only part of the
  attempt, or "ambiguous" if you cannot identify one clear operation.
  Every incomplete status needs exact nonblank unrepresented_spans
  quoting what one operation does not represent. Supply action_spans
  for identified operations; only ambiguous may have no action_spans.
  For every incomplete status, kind is "none", fields [], asks "none".
- Quoted report or request content is content, not extra acts by the
  speaker. Coordinated instruments of one act and expected knock-on
  effects do not make multiple acts. A goal achieved BY a concrete
  operation is not itself an additional operation. Bind the concrete
  means, preserving the person's expressed stance.
- For example, "withhold assent by recording a concern" is a
  concerned recording when that kind exists; it is not a withdrawal.
  Stance and assent are distinct. Withholding assent when assent is
  already false does not mean revoking or withdrawing prior assent.
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

asks.description: When the person asks, tells or orders someone else to do something rather than doing it themself, the entity id of the one asked; otherwise 'none'.

action_spans.description: Exact nonblank substrings naming the attempted operation.

unrepresented_spans.description: Exact nonblank substrings not represented by one operation.

fields.description: One row per field of the chosen kind; empty for 'wait' or 'none'.

quoted_span.description: The exact words of the attempt that name it.

value.description: An entity id for an entity field, else the value.

kind.description: The action kind this attempt is, 'wait' for doing nothing, or 'none' if no kind fits.

names.description: The entity id of every person or thing in the world the attempt's words name, the person themself left out; empty if it names none.

nearest_kind.description: When kind is 'none', the closest kind; otherwise the chosen kind.

why.description: One sentence on which words decided the kind.
